sourcedFrom: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) (2022)
cleanIntro: The book for this can is JK Armament's 195, 155 & 105 Series Operation and Maintenance Manual, which gives the 105 VERSAX .22 Cal its own section. It is a modular rimfire can, not a sealed one: a 1/2-28 thread mount, a 1.3 inch tube, four rimfire baffles and a flash cut end cap, all threaded together. JK's maintenance is short and the same for every can in the book: unthread each component, clean with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush, inspect, and thread it back together hand tight.

steps.title: Host unloaded and the action open first
steps.action: Before the can comes off, unload the host and open the action so you can see it is clear of ammunition. If you are not sure how to do that on your rifle or pistol, JK sends you to the firearm's own manual, a licensed dealer, its maker or a gunsmith.
steps.prose: This guide is for the suppressor. The host's own book is the authority on clearing the host.
steps.quote: WARNING: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.3

steps.title: It may be hot — gloves
steps.action: A can that has just been fired can burn you. Let it cool, or take it off in heat-resistant gloves, as JK directs.
steps.prose: A small aluminium can heats quickly over a long rimfire string.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use heat-resistant gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.3

steps.title: What it is rated for
steps.action: Confirm what has been through it. The 105 VERSAX .22 is JK's rimfire can, rated up to 5.7x28mm: full-auto with no minimum barrel on 22LR, 17 Mach 2, 17 HMR, 17 WSM, 22 Mag, 22 Hornet and 5.7x28mm.
steps.prose: Anything bigger than that list is outside its rating.
steps.quote: Designed for all of your rimfire shooting needs right on up to 5.7x28mm, the JK 105 VERSAX .22CAL is one of the very smallest and lightest silencers ever to hit the market!
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 3.10 JK 105 VERSAX .22 Cal, p.16

steps.title: Off the host
steps.action: Unthread the can from the barrel. Once it is off, JK recommends a thread protector or another muzzle device on the barrel to protect the threads and crown while the can is away.
steps.prose: Keep the thread mount with the can; it is part of the stack you will clean.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is removed from the host firearm, JK Armament recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.3

steps.title: Unthread each component
steps.action: Unthread the thread mount, the tube and the end cap, and take the four rimfire baffles out. Do it by hand where you can; JK allows a JK 105 series wrench if needed, or a crescent or combination wrench.
steps.prose: Lay the parts out in the order they came off. The book prints no stacking diagram, so your own layout is the record of how it goes back.
steps.quote: Unthread each component. Use a JK 155 or JK 105 series wrench to disassemble, if necessary. A crescent wrench or a combination wrench may also be used.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance — Disassembly, p.25

steps.title: Thread locker means heat first
steps.action: If Blue Loctite or another removable thread locker was used on any joint, that joint may need heating before it will come apart. Do not force it with the wrench cold.
steps.prose: A wrench on an aluminium tube that will not turn is how a tube gets crushed.
steps.quote: CAUTION: If Blue Loctite® or other removable thread locker was used, the unit may need to be heated prior to disassembly.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance — Disassembly, p.25
steps.warn: Never crank a locked joint cold — heat first.

steps.title: Ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush
steps.action: Clean every component with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush. That is JK's whole method for this can — nothing harsher is named.
steps.prose: The whole can is 7075 aluminium with a hard anodized finish, so a nylon brush, not steel.
steps.quote: JK Armament recommends cleaning your Mission Configurable Suppressor using CLP (ammonia free) and a nylon brush.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance, p.25

steps.title: Lead — protect yourself and dispose of it properly
steps.action: Expect lead and other toxic residue inside the can. Gloves on, clean away from food, and dispose of the dirty CLP and rags properly.
steps.prose: Rimfire ammunition is mostly lead bullets, so this can sees plenty of it.
steps.quote: Lead and other toxic materials may be deposited inside of your suppressor; use appropriate cautions and disposal methods when cleaning.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance, p.25

steps.title: Carbon off every thread and face
steps.action: Brush the carbon off the threads and the faces of every component — the thread mount, both ends of the tube, the end cap and each baffle face.
steps.prose: Carbon on a thread or a face is what stops a joint closing fully and what makes it seize next time.
steps.quote: Keep carbon deposits off of threads and faces of all components.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance, p.25

steps.title: Inspect every component and thread
steps.action: With everything clean, look at each component and each thread before anything goes back together.
steps.prose: A damaged thread, a cracked or bent baffle, or a dented tube does not go back in. JK's warranty and repair route is through its online RMA form.
steps.quote: Clean all components with an appropriate CLP (ammonia free) and a nylon brush. Inspect all components and threads.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance — Disassembly, p.25

steps.title: Clear and dry before it is fired
steps.action: Look through the bore: nothing in it. JK forbids firing through an obstructed suppressor, and a can that has been under water must drain completely first.
steps.prose: Mud, dirt or a rag fibre in the bore is an obstruction.
steps.quote: DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed suppressor. If submerged in water, the user must allow sufficient time to drain the suppressor completely.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.2
steps.warn: Never fire through an obstructed suppressor.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should have the can off the host and apart: thread mount, tube, four rimfire baffles and the flash cut end cap, each cleaned and inspected. Reassembly is next.
steps.prose: That is everything JK's book takes apart.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 3.10 JK 105 VERSAX .22 Cal — Includes, p.16

deepAbsentReason: There is no deeper clean for the 105 VERSAX .22. JK's maintenance section (p.25) gives one disassembly for every can in the book — unthread each component, clean with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush, inspect — and that is the field strip above. The book takes no component further apart and describes no other cleaning method.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES, TUBE & END CAP
tasks: Four rimfire baffles, the tube and the flash cut end cap
Ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush — JK's method
Do not use a cleaner containing ammonia
Gloves on: lead and other toxic residue; dispose of dirty CLP and rags properly

cleaning.name: THREADS & FACES
tasks: Carbon brushed off every component face

cleaning.name: MOUNT
tasks: The 1/2-28 thread mount cleaned and its threads inspected
The host's muzzle threads and shoulder cleaned so the mount seats fully

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: A can that was wet is drained completely
A thread protector or muzzle device on the host's barrel while the can is off

reassembly: Apply a light coat of CLP to the threads and inspect every component and thread before assembling.
Thread the components back together in the order you laid them out, taking care not to cross thread.
Hand tighten the components together. If you use a torque setting, do not exceed 10 ft/lbs; one drop of Blue 242 Loctite may be used for a more robust configuration.
Thread the can onto the host until the mount is fully shouldered on the barrel, with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the thread mount. Never use a crush washer.
Check the can is still secure after 30 rounds, and keep checking it often.
fncheck: Look through the bore: clear. The mount sits fully shouldered on the barrel with no visible gap and no crush washer. Every joint is hand tight with no cross threading, and the can is checked again for tightness after 30 rounds.
